name: Fiji oil dish
first: The outside measures 53 × 32.1 × 9.1 cm. The Met calls this wooden object an oil dish.
boundary: All three numbers are outside dimensions. The volume of the hollow stays open.
stake: The lower rail needs a mark for the outline. Someone has pencilled a proposed capacity in the margin.
lower: Halen traces the outside to leave room at the rail. The pouring line stays blank.
upper: Clio files an outline and a separate empty capacity field. A later reader can request a cavity measurement without changing the outside guide.
altText: A broad wooden dish with a carved openwork part at one end.

name: Long wooden ladle from the Austral Islands
first: The Met lists 137.2 cm high, 15.2 cm wide, and 14 cm deep.
boundary: The date is approximate. The three numbers describe this individual wooden ladle along different axes.
stake: A carrier has put all three arrows along the long side of her guide.
lower: Halen leaves a long-axis arrow for the next carrier. Smaller arrows stay in the Shelter reference.
upper: Clio lays the outline lengthwise and inserts a separate end tab for width and depth. Either view can be checked by number.
altText: A long, straight shaft ending in a dark, oval ladle bowl.

name: 239 cm tapa cloth from Fiji
first: The museum gives 239 cm by 79 cm and identifies paper mulberry bark.
boundary: Both numbers belong to this whole cloth. The latest possible making boundary is before 1971.
stake: The pull-out guide is pinned at one end, so readers can see its width but lose their place along the length.
lower: Halen sets a width mark at the low rail and keeps the accession by it. Someone can use the mark from either end.
upper: Clio leaves tick marks for both extents and a separate date bound. The catalogue copy can be retrieved when the guide folds away.
altText: A long rectangular cloth with banded dark and pale repeating motifs.

name: Narrow dark cloth from Hawaiʻi
first: The museum lists 106.4 by 18.5 cm. The dark strip appears narrow in the collection image.
boundary: The catalogue says probably paper mulberry bark. Its material wording stays tentative.
stake: The short copy has space for only one big line. A counter worker needs to identify this so it reaches the right drawer.
lower: Halen makes the 106.4 cm line easy to find and keeps “probably” in the material key.
upper: Clio stores the length line across from the tentative identification. Later readers can compare it with the wider strip.
altText: A narrow dark rectangular cloth with a divided surface.

name: 82.7 cm reddish cloth from Hawaiʻi
first: The extent is 82.7 by 37 cm. The collection view shows a broad red-brown surface.
boundary: The widths of this piece and the longer 106.4 cm strip are different. Both catalogues say probably paper mulberry bark.
stake: A sailor has put two cloth guides under the same width notch.
lower: Halen shifts this guide to its own 37 cm mark beside the old narrow mark.
upper: Clio sets the length and width side by side and keeps the number on this leaf. A reader can compare the guides without swapping names.
altText: A reddish rectangular cloth with fine repeating texture.

name: 147 cm reddish cloth from Hawaiʻi
first: The stated extent is 147 × 36.2 cm. The largest extent is along the red strip.
boundary: This is the museum record of one piece. Its full making date and precise source plant remain open.
stake: Two measurements hit almost the same width mark. The worker needs a second way to tell the slips apart.
lower: Halen adds a length tick to the description by the rail. Readers can find the longer slip even when width marks are close.
upper: Clio pairs the two axes on this accession leaf. The plant note keeps its question open for a later reading.
altText: A long cloth with a reddish centre and darker narrow edges.

name: Near-square cloth from Hawaiʻi
first: The catalogue gives 32.5 cm by 29 cm for this piece.
boundary: Nearly square is a convenient description. The exact dimensions differ by 3.5 cm.
stake: The rough drawing has equal sides. Halen must place a guide where someone can pass it on to a second reader.
lower: Halen adds the longer end tick to the rounded working description and uses that end for the handover.
upper: Clio keeps the two measured lines distinct on the indexed slip. The rough square stays in the comparison pocket.
altText: A short brown cloth with closely spaced pale markings.

name: Broad painted cloth from Hawaiʻi
first: The museum describes the cloth as painted and measures it at 133.4 × 125.7 cm.
boundary: Paper mulberry bark is a probable identification. A photograph can give a pattern view without resolving the fibre.
stake: A guest wants to tell a broad painted panel from a small strip after the pictures are printed at the same width.
lower: Halen makes the broad scale evident with separate edge ticks. The painted description stays with the accession.
upper: Clio stores a broad size diagram and a separate paint observation. Equal-size thumbnails can point to either without passing for a scale measure.
altText: A broad reddish-brown cloth with a dark geometric painted design.

name: Stilt footrest from the Marquesas Islands
first: The hardwood footrest is 40 cm high. The museum describes a slit at the back for a securing cord.
boundary: The number measures this detached footrest. The catalogue separately describes the taller stilt pole.
stake: The front view makes the footrest look like the whole object. A passing reader wants to know where the cord went.
lower: Halen adds a pointer around the back of the plain drawing while giving the projection its own size mark.
upper: Clio files separate tabs for the front outline and the back slit. A reader can follow the museum explanation of the fastening.
altText: A tall dark carved wooden footrest with an upward-curving platform.

name: Printed bark-cloth panel attributed to Samoa
attribution: Maker unrecorded. Museum lists Samoa with a question mark
first: The Cleveland Museum records a printed bark-cloth panel 90.2 × 153 cm.
boundary: Samoa is a tentative place attribution on this exact record.
stake: An unsigned label left the question mark behind when it was copied onto a room plan.
lower: Halen clips the question mark to the place line. The guide keeps its measured scale while the place is checked.
upper: Clio places the tentative place note in the same pocket as the print and its dimensions. A later edit will still see what needs evidence.
altText: A vertically photographed brown rectangular panel with fine repeating texture.

name: Masi kesa panels from interior Viti Levu
first: The Met lists bark cloth and pigment. The broad panel extent is 266.7 cm wide and 279.4 cm long.
boundary: The object is catalogued from Viti Levu. The owner line names a later holding in Samoa; that line describes custody.
stake: Two place tabs fell into the same loop. A carrier needs to know which place belongs with the making record.
lower: Halen ties the Viti Levu tab to the object guide. The separate holdings line stays visible in the Shelter.
upper: Clio opens two labelled place pockets so a reader can follow the making record and later custody independently.
altText: A broad dark and tan set of panels with contrasting borders and large square motifs.

name: Short stone adze blade attributed to the Cook Islands
attribution: Maker unrecorded. The Cook Islands attribution is tentative
first: The Met measures the stone blade at 4 3/8 inches high.
boundary: The number applies to the stone blade, with its handle open. The place and period are qualified.
stake: The two blade photos were enlarged to the same thumbnail height. A reader wants a useful comparison before departing.
lower: Halen adds a 4 3/8 inch mark to the shorter edge tracing and leaves the handle space empty.
upper: Clio indexes the short stone blade separately and keeps its date and place qualifiers by the height line.
altText: A small dark stone adze blade with a narrower top and flat lower edge.

name: Tall stone adze blade attributed to the Cook Islands
attribution: Maker unrecorded. The Cook Islands attribution is tentative
first: The Met gives a height of 7 7/8 inches for this stone blade.
boundary: The shared title and date range still describe two different accession records and two heights.
stake: The tall stone blade arrived under a short drawing of its neighbour. The reader is about to pass the guide along.
lower: Halen draws a new height mark with this blade’s number so the two short copies can travel apart.
upper: Clio links the two blade records in the binder and gives each a separate observed height. The shared caption can lead to either.
altText: A dark stone blade with a flared lower edge and a rounded narrower end.

name: ʻUkulele made about 1880
first: The Met lists mahogany, hardwood and metal. The instrument measures 52.1 × 14 × 4.5 cm.
boundary: A photo and these dimensions describe this instrument. A sound needs a separate recording or other evidence.
stake: Someone left a blank sound slot beside a photograph. The carrier wants to post a useful view while the sound slot stays open.
lower: Halen leaves the body and edge dimensions by the rail and marks the sound slot for a later source.
upper: Clio files the dimensions and material record with separate space for a future sound record of known provenance.
altText: A small wooden string instrument with a dark fingerboard and a round opening.

name: ʻŪkēkē from Hawaiʻi
first: The Met measures the greatest width of this wooden string instrument as 3.6 cm and its length as 53.9 cm.
boundary: The record lists wood and gut. Its greatest width marks its widest section, with narrower points elsewhere.
stake: The scale note slipped onto the narrow end of a diagram. A reader wants one handle for finding the widest point.
lower: Halen adds a small arrow for “greatest width” to the rail guide. The length keeps its own arrow.
upper: Clio leaves a full length guide and a crosswise greatest-width reference in two labelled leaves for the same accession.
altText: A slim brown string instrument showing a subtle curve.

name: Feathered ʻUlīʻulī from Hawaiʻi
dimensions: Height: 10 in. (25.4 cm) Diameter (Of gourd): 4 1/2 in. (11.4 cm) Diameter (Circular top): 11 in. (27.9 cm)
first: The Met lists a 27.9 cm circular top and an 11.4 cm gourd diameter. The materials include gourd and feathers.
boundary: The two diameters belong to different parts of this object. The catalogue date describes the object itself.
stake: The working profile shows a single circle. A fitter needs to see which circle the big measurement belongs to.
lower: Halen opens the larger circle beside a small gourd outline. The clip names both parts before the next person uses it.
upper: Clio saves the two circles at the same scale and labels both. The catalogue number links them if the leaves are separated.
altText: A brown gourd at the base of a wide circle of layered feathers.

name: Ipu hula from Hawaiʻi
first: The Met lists gourd, tapa cloth and breadfruit gum for this 76.2 cm-high example. The instrument form joins a smaller gourd to a larger one.
boundary: The materials have a catalogue source. What joins the gourds is hard to establish from the silhouette alone.
stake: At a low viewing rail, a guest has a useful profile but the join line could be copied as solid gourd.
lower: Halen leaves the join mark pointing to the catalogue materials. The silhouette stays ready for a passing reader.
upper: Clio files the profile and the materials as independent leaves. A reader can ask which detail comes from the written record.
altText: Two rounded brown gourd forms joined at a narrow point.

name: Bamboo instrument tentatively titled Rooria
place: New Ireland, Bismarck Archipelago, Papua New Guinea
first: The Met lists a 23.4 cm frame and 17 cm tongue, with bamboo, fibre and shell.
boundary: “Rooria?” is the museum’s tentative object name. The two length lines refer to separate parts.
stake: The loose outline could mix the tongue with the outer frame, and its title needs its question mark.
lower: Halen marks the long outer part next to a separate inner tongue line. The tentative name travels with the guide.
upper: Clio leaves two part measurements and the tentative title on indexed leaves. A later reader can retrieve and compare both.
altText: A narrow orange-brown bamboo instrument with a cord and a small shell.

name: Bamboo mouth harp possibly from Aotearoa New Zealand
attribution: Maker unrecorded. Museum place attribution tentative
first: The Met lists 19.2 cm for the bamboo frame and 15.5 cm for its tongue.
boundary: The catalogue gives New Zealand with a question mark. A part measurement settles neither the place nor the name a maker used.
stake: A book in the shelter has two nearly alike frame sketches. This one needs its shorter frame measure and qualified place to stay attached.
lower: Halen adds the 19.2 cm frame line and puts “possibly” on the same side as the place.
upper: Clio sets the tongue and frame on separate lines and keeps the museum’s tentative place in the provenance pocket.
altText: A slender amber bamboo instrument with a long slot in the middle.

catalogTitle: New Caledonia: Large native hut on the road from Balade to Puebo, 1845, from "The Voyage to New Zealand (1842–46)"
name: Etching of a building on the Balade–Puebo road
place: Balade–Puebo road, New Caledonia, in the subject of the print
date: Etching made in 1863. Its title gives 1845 for the view.
first: Meryon’s etching is dated 1863. Its catalogue title names a building on the Balade–Puebo road and gives 1845 for the view.
boundary: The dates apply to the print and the pictured view. The museum entry does not give the builders’ names.
stake: One hook is labelled “date”. The harbour survey reader needs to tell a pictured date from a print date.
lower: Halen adds an upper date for the titled view and leaves the print date beside the carrying line.
upper: Clio sets the 1845 subject and 1863 print in two dated pockets and leaves a space for information from the people who built it.
altText: A wide monochrome etching showing buildings and vegetation beside an open route.

catalogTitle: The Island of Moorea Looking across the Strait from Tahiti, January 1891
name: Moorea across the strait in January 1891
place: Moorea seen from Tahiti, in the title of the painting
date: Making, 1891. The title gives January for the view.
medium: Watercolor, gouache and graphite on heavy tan wove paper
first: The Met describes a January 1891 view from Tahiti across the strait to Moorea. The painting is watercolour, gouache and graphite on tan wove paper.
boundary: The labelled viewpoint describes one artist’s view. A survey uses separate field measurements for height and colour.
stake: A lookout uses direction arrows. If the copy loses “from Tahiti”, the reader may stand on the wrong shore.
lower: Halen turns the direction line toward Moorea and pins the observer’s side by it. The painting stays linked as the source of that viewpoint.
upper: Clio keeps the view arrow and material line in the same numbered pocket, with a separate place for later measurements.
altText: A horizontal watercolour with bands of sea, island and pale sky.

catalogTitle: Double Study of Dawn, Moorea Seen across the Water, Tahiti
name: Two dawn studies across the water from Tahiti
place: Moorea seen from Tahiti, in the title of the studies
medium: Watercolor, gouache and graphite on laid paper
first: The Met groups two studies at 67.55.176a, b. The watercolour, gouache and graphite are on laid paper.
boundary: Two panels sit together under one catalogue entry. They have the same year, with no minute-by-minute scale in this record.
stake: A watch keeper thought two views could be turned into a timed change. The source has two panels and one year.
lower: Halen keeps both panels on the guide and omits a guessed interval from the working sheet.
upper: Clio files the two-part accession together. A separate interval field can accept a new source if one turns up.
altText: Two narrow greyscale island studies shown one above the other.

name: Punt crossing at Seymour
place: Seymour, Australia, in the catalogue title
first: The Met records albumen silver prints as a pair on an 8.5 × 17.3 cm mount. The title locates a punt at Seymour.
boundary: The measured surface is the photograph mount. It places no size marks on the actual crossing.
stake: A dock worker has used the heading “width at Seymour” for the width of the mount.
lower: Halen corrects the working width heading to “mount”. The punt’s width remains an open question at the reader’s mark.
upper: Clio keeps the two photographs together and files mount size away from the river description. The reader can use each measurement for its own purpose.
altText: A stereograph mount holding two similar brown views of a river crossing.

catalogTitle: Presqu'île de Banks, Pointe des Charbonniers, Akaroa (Seine fishing off Colliers' Point, Akaroa, Banks Peninsula, 1845), from "The Voyage to New Zealand (1842–46)"
name: Etched view of seine fishing off Colliers’ Point
place: Colliers’ Point, Akaroa, Aotearoa New Zealand, in the title of the view
date: Etching and drypoint dated 1863 and later. Title dates its scene to 1845.
first: The printed Akaroa view is dated 1863 and later. Its catalogue title dates the fishing scene to 1845.
boundary: The plate record measures 15.6 × 32.5 cm. It records a plate and its subject, with no count of catches.
stake: The upper binder has space for both a print date and a scene date. The working rail needs to avoid reusing one date for both.
lower: Halen keeps 1845 by the view and puts the impression date on a separate clip. The catch tally stays empty.
upper: Clio indexes the two date fields and stores the plate size with the edition. A reader can return to the exact impression.
altText: A wide monochrome printed scene of a coast and distant hills with small figures near the water.
